text:
olivia: promo hold on canary. integration-build-99 failed fetching release bundle: HTTP 410 Gone when curling https://artifacts.redwood/internal/bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip
deploy-bot: [automated] Promo hold applied to canary-2026-04-02. job=integration-build-99 exit=1 reason=artifact-410
sam: log snippet: `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 410 Gone` when trying to download bundle-v2.5.1.zip from artifacts.redwood/internal/bundles/
ci-bot: expected path present in manifest: `bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip -> s3://ci-artifacts/bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip` but HEAD returned 410.
luis: 410 usually means object was deleted or lifecycle expired. we had the bucket lifecycle sweep last night at 02:00 and any untagged objects older than 7d were removed. maybe upload didn't set retention/protected tag.
olivia: can we reupload quickly? I have a local copy of the bundle from packing host if owners agree. reupload+retry would unblock but might take ~12m.
release-manager: timeline: cut window closes in 18m. options: (A) reupload and retry (12-20m risk), (B) pin canary to previous successful bundle (5m), (C) abort cut. prefer minimal user impact: pin if <5m, otherwise reupload and delay cut.
sam: pinning process: `deploybot pin canary --image last-good-canary-2026-03-30 --reason "artifact missing bundle-v2.5.1.zip"` should be quick but needs agreement from release-owner.
ops: another approach: if reupload is safe and we can mark object protected right away, do reupload but set token and index register so runners see it. command: `aws s3 cp /tmp/bundle-v2.5.1.zip s3://ci-artifacts/bundles/ && aws s3api put-object-tagging --bucket ci-artifacts --key bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=protected,Value=true}]' && curl -XPOST https://artifacts.redwood/internal/index/register -d '{"key":"bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip"}' && deploybot retry integration-build-99`
ci-bot: note: if index registration lags, runners may still hit 404/410. index registration must succeed before retry.
luis: I'm pinging the packager host to confirm artifact integrity; if olivia has a verified copy, reupload now.
olivia: i have verified copy and can reupload now. running upload
olivia: (runs) `aws s3 cp bundle-v2.5.1.zip s3://ci-artifacts/bundles/`
olivia: done. tagging protected
olivia: (runs) `aws s3api put-object-tagging --bucket ci-artifacts --key bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=protected,Value=true}]'`
olivia: tagging applied. posting index register now
olivia: (runs) `curl -XPOST https://artifacts.redwood/internal/index/register -d '{"key":"bundles/bundle-v2.5.1.zip","etag":"zz-789"}'`
ops: index returned 200. triggering retry: `deploybot retry integration-build-99`
deploy-bot: retry queued for integration-build-99. runner=ci-runner-11
ci-bot: integration-build-99 started on ci-runner-11
ci-bot: download -> 200 OK, checksum matches expected sha256, unpack OK
ci-bot: tests: integration suite started... (progress)
(8m later)
ci-bot: integration-build-99 exit=0
deploy-bot: canary promo resumed automatically after job success. Promo status: hold -> queued promote.
release-manager: good work. will proceed with canary promote at 14:42 UTC. leaving release note: transient lifecycle sweep removed unprotected bundle; we reuploaded and protected object to unblock promo. follow-up: uploader must set protected tag and ensure index register completes atomically before lifecycle window.
luis: filed INF-789: ensure packager sets protected tag on upload and calls index/register in same transaction; add post-upload verification to CI.
ops: added short runbook to eng-releases: on artifact-410 during promo hold -> attempt reupload with protected tag+index register, retry build; fallback to deploybot pin to last-good canary if upload not possible within change window.
release-manager: thanks everyone. marking resolved when promote finishes :thumbsup:
